method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: Up for the fluid frame. The shell stopped being a fixed 672px box and became a frame that grows to config/appearance.json frame.reading_max_px, and the reading measure moved off the shell onto the title, the summary and the reader note - measured 2026-08-28, one max-w-2xl on the root layout capped every page at 624px and left 912px of a 1536px screen empty. The bytes are the item's own scoped rule: a one-column grid that becomes a body and a sticky meta rail above 1024px, so source, date and confidence stop interrupting the read. Read as a difference: origin/main's source built on this tree, this machine and this node read within 13 B of every record, so this is the change and not the toolchain. The frame VALUES cost nothing here - they are generated into src/styles/frame.generated.css at build time, because injecting them from the layout head instead was measured at 397 to 700 B of JavaScript on every route, including two that render nothing. Every route pays a few tens of bytes for the chart engine existing, without carrying any of it. Measured 2026-08-29 on one machine in one session, origin/main built first and this branch second: / 49,715 -> 49,738, /404 40,769 -> 40,802, /<date>/ 49,591 -> 49,610, /<date>/<topic>/ 49,684 -> 49,702, /archive/ 51,114 -> 51,137, /evals/ 41,725 -> 41,754. On the CI runner, a newer node, the same difference reads 72 to 77 B, which is what pushed /404 2 B past the 64 B tolerance and is why these records moved at all. The module count is unchanged on every route - /404 carries the same 14 modules before and after - so this is not chart code reaching a reading page. It is the shared entry chunk: adding a lazily-imported chunk grows the client manifest the entry embeds, and every route preloads the entry. That is the price of the engine being lazy rather than eager, and it is the right side of the trade: the alternative puts 153,204 B on the console first load instead of 30 B on each page. Up for the icon set. Fifteen glyphs, 2,128 B of marks, reach every route as one generated module because a component names an icon by id and the lookup cannot be tree-shaken on a dynamic key. Measured 2026-08-29 on this tree: / +1,897, /404 +1,771, /<date>/ +1,900, /<date>/<topic>/ +1,900, /archive/ +1,833, /console/ +1,404, /evals/ +1,775. The alternative measured against it was an inline sprite referenced by <use>, which costs no JavaScript at all but puts about 700 B of gzipped markup into every prerendered document - and /404 had 37 B of headroom under its ceiling, so that arm would have had to raise the one ceiling whose whole purpose is keeping the error page tiny. The bytes go where there is room for them. Up for installability. The shell gained a manifest link, an apple-touch-icon link and two media-scoped theme-color tags, plus the code that writes one unconditional theme-color from the resolved background - measured 2026-08-29, 126 to 131 B of first-load JS on every route and 271 B of gzipped markup in every prerendered document. Both are shell costs and neither is avoidable per page: app.html is shared. The apple-touch link in particular cannot be dropped, because Safari probes the ORIGIN root for that filename and this site is served from a project path. DOWN 127 to 150 B, and one module lighter, for the chart vocabulary landing on the console. Measured 2026-08-29: / 51,762 -> 51,613, /404 42,703 -> 42,576, /<date>/ 51,637 -> 51,487, /<date>/<topic>/ 51,728 -> 51,580, /archive/ 53,097 -> 52,961, /evals/ 43,658 -> 43,530, each losing a module from its preload list. The cause is chunking rather than deletion: with five more console-only chart modules in the graph, the bundler stopped hoisting the Chart component into the shared chunk and put it in the console chunk where its only callers now are. The ratchet is two-sided on purpose, so a route getting lighter is recorded rather than left as slack for the next regression to land inside. Up 774 B for the archive coming inside: a strip of the six most recent days at the foot of the digest, and the empty state rebuilt with the panel language everything else already had. Measured 2026-08-29. The strip carries dates and story counts only - it grows per day, never per story, which is what keeps it affordable on a page that also carries a whole day of articles. /archive/ is unchanged and is not deleted: it is a bookmarkable URL that works, and removing it to tidy the route list would spend a reader bookmark to buy nothing they can see.

/archive/.why: Up for the fluid frame and the archive's columns. The archive is the one list on the site that goes multi-column: it is a scan surface where a reader is finding the story they remember, so "find it fast" outranks the ranked order the digest has to protect. /console/.why: Runtime and shell plus the console route: hand-written SVG charts and the d3-scale and d3-array arithmetic behind them, the stage-timing decade axis with its minor stubs and its gap-instead-of-plunge run splitting, the compression scatter that places its articles in the browser, the Charts table that says what the router cost and what it published on each day, and the What the model did table. Up 1,854 B, which is 2.7 percent of the route, for the chart engine arriving: the Chart component, the funnel option builder and the token-to-sentinel bridge. About 40 B of that is the toolchain rather than the change - every unrelated route on this machine and this node read 36 to 63 B above its record in the same build, so the change itself is close to 1,810 B. The engine is NOT in this number. It is a lazy chunk of 153,204 B gzipped (451,227 B raw), fetched only when a chart hydrates, and no page anywhere preloads it - frontend/tests/charts.spec.ts fails the build if one ever does. Registering only the funnel, the tooltip and the SVG renderer is what makes that number affordable: importing the same package whole read 345,959 B gzipped (1,044,275 B raw) for the same one chart, so the registration list in src/lib/charts/core.ts is worth 56 percent of the download. The console gains a funnel over reached, asked, drafted and published, drawn to SVG in Node at build time, so it is on the page with no JavaScript at all and follows a theme change because its colours leave as custom-property references rather than hexes. The prerendered console document is 150,060 B gzip -9 over the committed ledger, against a ceiling of 301,580, leaving 151,520 spare. Up for the icon set. Fifteen glyphs, 2,128 B of marks, reach every route as one generated module because a component names an icon by id and the lookup cannot be tree-shaken on a dynamic key. Both are shell costs and neither is avoidable per page: app.html is shared. The apple-touch link in particular cannot be dropped, because Safari probes the ORIGIN root for that filename and this site is served from a project path. Up 3,148 B for the chart vocabulary: a donut gauge, a target bar, a waterfall, stacked bars, a sparkline and the KPI card that carries one. Measured 2026-08-29. Six shapes because there are six questions - one shape repeated six times is what made this page read as a single grey instrument. The arithmetic behind each is a pure function tested without a browser (frontend/tests/vocabulary.spec.ts recomputes every geometry independently); the drawing belongs to the engine and is not ours to test. The engine chunk itself is unchanged in kind - still lazy, still console-only - though it now registers the bar, line and pie types plus the grid, legend and mark-line components those shapes need.
